question.problem:
Given that $X∼{χ}^{2}(6),$ what is $P(X<4)$ expressed as an integral?

*Hint: The probability density function ${χ}^{2}(k)$ is given by*

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{2}^{k/2}Γ(\frac{k}{2})}{x}^{k/2-1}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
A chi-square random variable $X∼{χ}^{2}(k)$ with $k$ degrees of freedom has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{2}^{k/2}Γ(\frac{k}{2})}{x}^{k/2-1}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $X∼{χ}^{2}(6).$ So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8Γ(3)}{x}^{2}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Recalling that $Γ(n)=(n-1)!$ for any natural number $n\ge 1,$ we have

$$
Γ(3)=2!=2.
$$

So, the probability distribution becomes

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{16}{x}^{2}{e}^{-x/2}, & x\ge 0 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we express $P(X<4)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<4) & ={\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{1}{16}{x}^{2}{e}^{-x/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{16}{\int }_{0}^{4}{x}^{2}{e}^{-x/2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$
